<ROLE>
Your primary role is to assist users by executing commands, modifying code, and solving technical problems effectively. You should be thorough, methodical, and prioritize quality over speed.
* If the user asks a question, like "why is X happening", don't try to fix the problem. Just give an answer to the question.
</ROLE>

<EFFICIENCY>
* Each action you take is somewhat expensive. Wherever possible, combine multiple actions into a single action, e.g. combine multiple bash commands into one, using sed and grep to edit/view multiple files at once.
* When exploring the codebase, use efficient tools like find, grep, and git commands with appropriate filters to minimize unnecessary operations.
</EFFICIENCY>

<FILE_SYSTEM_GUIDELINES>
* When a user provides a file path, do NOT assume it's relative to the current working directory. First explore the file system to locate the file before working on it.
* If asked to edit a file, edit the file directly, rather than creating a new file with a different filename.
* For global search-and-replace operations, consider using `sed` instead of opening file editors multiple times.
* NEVER create multiple versions of the same file with different suffixes (e.g., file_test.py, file_fix.py, file_simple.py). Instead:
  - Always modify the original file directly when making changes
  - If you need to create a temporary file for testing, delete it once you've confirmed your solution works
  - If you decide a file you created is no longer useful, delete it instead of creating a new version
* Do NOT include documentation files explaining your changes in version control unless the user explicitly requests it

</FILE_SYSTEM_GUIDELINES>

<CODE_QUALITY>
* Write clean, efficient code with minimal comments. Avoid redundancy in comments: Do not repeat information that can be easily inferred from the code itself.
* When implementing solutions, focus on making the minimal changes needed to solve the problem.
* Before implementing any changes, first thoroughly understand the codebase through exploration.
* If you are adding a lot of code to a function or file, consider splitting the function or file into smaller pieces when appropriate.
* Place all imports at the top of the file unless explicitly requested otherwise or if placing imports at the top would cause issues (e.g., circular imports, conditional imports, or imports that need to be delayed for specific reasons).
</CODE_QUALITY>

<VERSION_CONTROL>
* If there are existing git user credentials already configured, use them and add Co-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev> to any commits messages you make. if a git config doesn't exist use "openhands" as the user.name and "openhands@all-hands.dev" as the user.email by default, unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

</VERSION_CONTROL>

<PULL_REQUESTS>

* When creating pull requests, create only ONE per session/issue unless explicitly instructed otherwise.
* When working with an existing PR, update it with new commits rather than creating additional PRs for the same issue.
* When updating a PR, preserve the original PR title and purpose, updating description only when necessary.
</PULL_REQUESTS>

<PROBLEM_SOLVING_WORKFLOW>
1. EXPLORATION: Thoroughly explore relevant files and understand the context before proposing solutions
2. ANALYSIS: Consider multiple approaches and select the most promising one
3. TESTING:
   * For bug fixes: Create tests to verify issues before implementing fixes

<SECURITY>

<EXTERNAL_SERVICES>

</EXTERNAL_SERVICES>

<TROUBLESHOOTING>

```
  "name": "Message",

      "type": "long",
      "aliases": ["oldname"],
      "doc": "test"
    }

}
```

fields get ordered with default values last
```
    someotherfield: int = dataclasses.field(metadata={'aliases': ['oldname']})
    fieldwithdefault: str = "some default value"
```

   111	### Serialization to avro or avro-json and json payload
   112	
   113	For serialization is neccesary to use python class/dataclasses instance
   114	
   115	```python
   116	from dataclasses import dataclass
   117	
   118	import typing
   119	
   120	from dataclasses_avroschema import AvroModel
   121	
   122	
   123	@dataclass
   124	class Address(AvroModel):
   125	    "An Address"
   126	    street: str
   127	    street_number: int
   128	
   129	
   130	@dataclass
   131	class User(AvroModel):
   132	    "User with multiple Address"
   133	    name: str
   134	    age: int
   135	    addresses: typing.List[Address]
   136	
   137	address_data = {
   138	    "street": "test",
   139	    "street_number": 10,
   140	}
   141	
   142	# create an Address instance
   143	address = Address(**address_data)
   144	
   145	data_user = {
   146	    "name": "john",
   147	    "age": 20,
   148	    "addresses": [address],
   149	}
   150	
   151	# create an User instance
   152	user = User(**data_user)
   153	
   154	user.serialize()
   155	# >>> b"\x08john(\x02\x08test\x14\x00"
   156	
   157	user.serialize(serialization_type="avro-json")
   158	# >>> b'{"name": "john", "age": 20, "addresses": [{"street": "test", "street_number": 10}]}'
   159	
   160	# Get the json from the instance
   161	user.to_json()
   162	# >>> '{"name": "john", "age": 20, "addresses": [{"street": "test", "street_number": 10}]}'
   163	
   164	# Get a python dict
   165	user.to_dict()
   166	# >>> {"name": "john", "age": 20, "addresses": [{"street": "test", "street_number": 10}]}
   167	
   168	```

   170	### Deserialization
   171	
   172	Deserialization could take place with an instance dataclass or the dataclass itself. Can return the dict representation or a new class instance
   173	
   174	```python
   175	import typing
   176	import dataclasses
   177	
   178	from dataclasses_avroschema import AvroModel
   179	
   180	
   181	@dataclasses.dataclass
   182	class Address(AvroModel):
   183	    "An Address"
   184	    street: str
   185	    street_number: int
   186	
   187	@dataclasses.dataclass
   188	class User(AvroModel):
   189	    "User with multiple Address"
   190	    name: str
   191	    age: int
   192	    addresses: typing.List[Address]
   193	
   194	avro_binary = b"\x08john(\x02\x08test\x14\x00"
   195	avro_json_binary = b'{"name": "john", "age": 20, "addresses": [{"street": "test", "street_number": 10}]}'
   196	
   197	# return a new class instance!!
   198	User.deserialize(avro_binary)
   199	# >>>> User(name='john', age=20, addresses=[Address(street='test', street_number=10)])
   200	
   201	# return a python dict
   202	User.deserialize(avro_binary, create_instance=False)
   203	# >>> {"name": "john", "age": 20, "addresses": [{"street": "test", "street_number": 10}]}
   204	
   205	# return a new class instance!!
   206	User.deserialize(avro_json_binary, serialization_type="avro-json")
   207	# >>>> User(name='john', age=20, addresses=[Address(street='test', street_number=10)])
   208	
   209	# return a python dict
   210	User.deserialize(avro_json_binary, serialization_type="avro-json", create_instance=False)
   211	# >>> {"name": "john", "age": 20, "addresses": [{"street": "test", "street_number": 10}]}
   212	```

   214	## Pydantic integration
   215	
   216	To add `dataclasses-avroschema` functionality to `pydantic` you only need to replace `BaseModel` by `AvroBaseModel`:
   217	
   218	```python
   219	import typing
   220	import enum
   221	import dataclasses
   222	
   223	from dataclasses_avroschema.avrodantic import AvroBaseModel
   224	
   225	from pydantic import Field
   226	
   227	
   228	class FavoriteColor(str, enum.Enum):
   229	    BLUE = "BLUE"
   230	    YELLOW = "YELLOW"
   231	    GREEN = "GREEN"
   232	
   233	
   234	@dataclasses.dataclass
   235	class UserAdvance(AvroBaseModel):
   236	    name: str
   237	    age: int
   238	    pets: typing.List[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["dog", "cat"])
   239	    accounts: typing.Dict[str, int] = Field(default_factory=lambda: {"key": 1})
   240	    has_car: bool = False
   241	    favorite_colors: FavoriteColor = FavoriteColor.BLUE
   242	    country: str = "Argentina"
   243	    address: str = None
   244	
   245	    class Meta:
   246	        schema_doc = False
   247	
   248	
   249	# Avro schema
   250	UserAdvance.avro_schema()
   251	'{
   252	    "type": "record",
   253	    "name": "UserAdvance",
   254	    "fields": [
   255	        {"name": "name", "type": "string"},
   256	        {"name": "age", "type": "long"},
   257	        {"name": "pets", "type": {"type": "array", "items": "string", "name": "pet"}, "default": ["dog", "cat"]},
   258	        {"name": "accounts", "type": {"type": "map", "values": "long", "name": "account"}, "default": {"key": 1}},
   259	        {"name": "has_car", "type": "boolean", "default": false},
   260	        {"name": "favorite_colors", "type": {"type": "enum", "name": "favorite_color", "symbols": ["BLUE", "YELLOW", "GREEN"]}, "default": "BLUE"},
   261	        {"name": "country", "type": "string", "default": "Argentina"},
   262	        {"name": "address", "type": ["null", "string"], "default": null}
   263	    ]
   264	}'
   265	
   266	# Json schema
   267	UserAdvance.json_schema()
   268	
   269	{
   270	    "title": "UserAdvance",
   271	    "description": "UserAdvance(*, name: str, age: int, pets: List[str] = None, ...",
   272	    "type": "object",
   273	    "properties": {
   274	        "name": {"title": "Name", "type": "string"},
   275	        "age": {"title": "Age", "type": "integer"},
   276	        "pets": {"title": "Pets", "type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
   277	        "accounts": {"title": "Accounts", "type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "integer"}},
   278	        "has_car": {"title": "Has Car", "default": false, "type": "boolean"},
   279	        "favorite_colors": {"default": "BLUE", "allOf": [{"$ref": "#/definitions/FavoriteColor"}]},
   280	        "country": {"title": "Country", "default": "Argentina", "type": "string"},
   281	        "address": {"title": "Address", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["name", "age"], "definitions": {"FavoriteColor": {"title": "FavoriteColor", "description": "An enumeration.", "enum": ["BLUE", "YELLOW", "GREEN"], "type": "string"}}
   282	}
   283	
   284	user = UserAdvance(name="bond", age=50)
   285	
   286	# pydantic
   287	user.dict()
   288	# >>> {'name': 'bond', 'age': 50, 'pets': ['dog', 'cat'], 'accounts': {'key': 1}, 'has_car': False, 'favorite_colors': <FavoriteColor.BLUE: 'BLUE'>, 'country': 'Argentina', 'address': None}
   289	
   290	# pydantic
   291	user.json()
   292	# >>> '{"name": "bond", "age": 50, "pets": ["dog", "cat"], "accounts": {"key": 1}, "has_car": false, "favorite_colors": "BLUE", "country": "Argentina", "address": null}'
   293	
   294	# pydantic
   295	user = UserAdvance(name="bond")
   296	
   297	# ValidationError: 1 validation error for UserAdvance
   298	# age
   299	# field required (type=value_error.missing)
   300	
   301	
   302	# dataclasses-avroschema
   303	event = user.serialize()
   304	print(event)
   305	# >>> b'\x08bondd\x04\x06dog\x06cat\x00\x02\x06key\x02\x00\x00\x00\x12Argentina\x00'
   306	
   307	UserAdvance.deserialize(data=event)
   308	# >>> UserAdvance(name='bond', age=50, pets=['dog', 'cat'], accounts={'key': 1}, has_car=False, favorite_colors=<FavoriteColor.BLUE: 'BLUE'>, country='Argentina', address=None)
   309	```

   311	## Examples with python streaming drivers (kafka and redis)
   312	
   313	Under [examples](https://github.com/marcosschroh/dataclasses-avroschema/tree/master/examples) folder you can find 3 differents kafka examples, one with [aiokafka](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiokafka) (`async`) showing the simplest use case when a `AvroModel` instance is serialized and sent it thorught kafka, and the event is consumed.
   314	The other two examples are `sync` using the [kafka-python](https://github.com/dpkp/kafka-python) driver, where the `avro-json` serialization and `schema evolution` (`FULL` compatibility) is shown.
   315	Also, there are two `redis` examples using `redis streams` with [walrus](https://github.com/coleifer/walrus) and [redisgears-py](https://github.com/RedisGears/redisgears-py)
   316	
   317	## Factory and fixtures
   318	
   319	[Dataclasses Avro Schema](https://github.com/marcosschroh/dataclasses-avroschema) also includes a `factory` feature, so you can generate `fast` python instances and use them, for example, to test your data streaming pipelines. Instances can be generated using the `fake` method.
   320	
   321	*Note*: This feature is not enabled by default and requires you have the `faker` extra installed. You may install it with `pip install 'dataclasses-avroschema[faker]'`
   322	
   323	
   324	```python
   325	import typing
   326	import dataclasses
   327	
   328	from dataclasses_avroschema import AvroModel
   329	
   330	
   331	@dataclasses.dataclass
   332	class Address(AvroModel):
   333	    "An Address"
   334	    street: str
   335	    street_number: int
   336	
   337	
   338	@dataclasses.dataclass
   339	class User(AvroModel):
   340	    "User with multiple Address"
   341	    name: str
   342	    age: int
   343	    addresses: typing.List[Address]
   344	
   345	
   346	Address.fake()
   347	# >>>> Address(street='PxZJILDRgbXyhWrrPWxQ', street_number=2067)
   348	
   349	User.fake()
   350	# >>>> User(name='VGSBbOGfSGjkMDnefHIZ', age=8974, addresses=[Address(street='vNpPYgesiHUwwzGcmMiS', street_number=4790)])
   351	```
